sentences.text: Cardiodon is a herbivorous sauropod genus known from a single tooth found in the Middle Jurassic Forest Marble Formation of Wiltshire, England.
The known tooth of Cardiodon is spatulate with a slight convexity on its inner side, a rare combination.
The tooth crown is short and wide, slightly curved inward, with an outer side strongly convex from front to rear.
A shallow groove runs parallel to the rear edge on the outer side of the tooth crown.
The tooth crown tapers toward its tip and lacks denticles on its edges.
The enamel of the tooth shows small wrinkles, which is the feature referenced by the specific name rugulosus.
Although only known from teeth, a probable body length of 16 meters has been estimated for Cardiodon.
Richard Owen assigned the specific name rugulosus, meaning "wrinkled", to the species in 1844.
Cardiodon was the first sauropod genus to receive a formal name, although the describer was unaware of its classification at the time.
Fossils of Cardiodon were found in the Forest Marble and Great Oolite formations near Wiltshire and Gloucestershire, England.
As a sauropod, Cardiodon was likely a large, quadrupedal herbivore, though scanty remains limit further details.
Recent analyses suggest Cardiodon is a distinct genus possibly related to Turiasaurus, though it was historically often referred to as Cetiosaurus.
Cardiodon was previously classified within the Cetiosauridae family or its own family, Cardiodontidae.
Cardiodon teeth differ from Cetiosaurus teeth because they possess a convex lingual face.
Cardiodon rugulosus lived approximately 167 million years ago during the Middle Jurassic Bathonian stage in what is now Europe.
The genus Cardiodon existed between 168.2 and 165.3 million years ago during the Bathonian stage.

Researchers Upchurch and Martin (2003) argued that Cardiodon should be retained as a distinct genus because the teeth differ from those of Cetiosaurus oxoniensis and lack evidence linking them to that skeleton.
Upchurch et al. (2004) found that Cardiodon teeth possess autapomorphies distinct from those of eusauropods, supporting its separation.
